proof: At the domain points $\varnothing$ and $[n]$, every universal hypothesis has the common value 0 or 1, respectively, so neither is effective. For every proper nonempty subset $A\subset[n]$, choose $i\in A$ and $j\notin A$; then $u_i(A)=1$ and $u_j(A)=0$. Thus all and only the other $2^n-2$ points are effective (also for $n=1$, when this number is zero).
name: Effective Range of Universal Class
